evidence.title: atrium FAQ
evidence.finding: Free public beta; macOS 12+ and Windows 10/11, Linux desktop planned. App closed, SDK MIT. Agents run on owning machines.

evidence.title: Tasks and runs
evidence.finding: Project task records have stable numbers, metadata, comments and distinct runs. Local/remote daemon schedules and resumes runs; review and completion states are separate.

evidence.title: HQ directors and routines
evidence.finding: Product-owned directors keep persistent conversations, delegate work and use recurring routines; results still need review.

evidence.title: Locations
evidence.finding: Linux SSH or paired Mac/Windows hosts own repository, sessions, credentials and scheduler. Unreachable hosts become read-only, not local fallbacks.

evidence.title: atriumd
evidence.finding: Daemon owns PTYs and sessions; detach preserves work, explicit full quit ends runtime. A host must remain awake/running.

evidence.title: Persistence and recovery
evidence.finding: Workspace state, task/run SQLite, review SQLite and terminal history are persisted. A reboot restores state but does not preserve live processes.

evidence.title: Agent messaging
evidence.finding: Framed cross-pane/location messages include sender/reply identity. Unconfirmed delivery requires timeline confirmation before retry.

evidence.title: Source control
evidence.finding: Integrated staging/commit/branch actions, hunk comments in review.db and send-to-agent review follow-up.

evidence.title: Telemetry
evidence.finding: Core lifecycle telemetry on by default; detailed analytics and crash reports require opt-in. Send nothing disables both; agent-provider traffic is separate.

evidence.title: Adapter SDK
evidence.finding: JSON manifest plus shell scripts define discovery, launch, resume, session enumeration and hooks; integration depth varies.

evidence.title: Adapter registry
evidence.finding: Registry lists official Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Pi, Grok, Antigravity and other adapters with platform and minimum-app version metadata.

evidence.title: Claude launch flags
evidence.finding: Selected skip-permissions uses upstream bypass; under root it sets a special environment flag and acceptEdits. The adapter sets model/effort and extra arguments.

evidence.title: Claude guard hook
evidence.finding: Calls atrium guard check for shell-class tools; errors are ignored for older CLIs. Policy evaluation is in closed core.

evidence.title: Codex launch and resume
evidence.finding: Resume appends resume and exact session ID, preserving selected model/effort and permission flags. This relies on upstream session history.

evidence.title: Product skill
evidence.finding: Skill describes progress digests, question wakeups, worktree setup with operation IDs and limits, and idempotent named workspace services. Instruction text does not independently prove backend enforcement.

evidence.title: HQ command contract
evidence.finding: Public instructions describe director/staff delegation, model profiles, reports, concurrency readouts, notebook expiry, playbook revisions and connector policy. The closed daemon implements these contracts; these instructions do not prove its enforcement.

evidence.title: Usage query contract
evidence.finding: Usage-enabled builds query local indexed estimates with coverage/as-of metadata, run/director attribution, live boards and JSON board export. This is not a provider invoice.

evidence.title: Shared transcript usage reader
evidence.finding: Reads local transcript events with checkpoint CRC validation, dedupe and missing/error accounting; shared usage_stream.py supports plain or compressed local transcripts. The reader emits local records, not vendor analytics.

evidence.title: Connector and companion package contract
evidence.finding: Public catalog supplies pinned local packages and remote MCP presets, secret references, requested OAuth scopes, policy defaults and companion rules; compiled core owns routing, approval and token injection.

evidence.title: Claude context injection
evidence.finding: Posts native hook payloads to loopback, receives pane context and fails open on missing tools, daemon or timeout. Hooks separately install scoped skill/director context and notebook requests.

evidence.title: Memory and consolidation
evidence.finding: Documented facts have scopes and successor history; opt-in consolidation has checkpointed windows and scoped token budgets. Self-improvement review is default, with optional guarded auto trials.

evidence.title: CLI command reference
evidence.finding: Documents task claims, runs, local IPC/headless behavior, remote routing, stored reviews, notes, agent moves, profiles, diagnostics and capture controls.

evidence.title: Project search
